reason: Notice of extension 90 days before the Lease Period ends. A step under the contract; nothing about claims or courts.

The Lessor sold the cafeteria goodwill to the Lessee and restrains itself within the Building and 500 m (a specified local limit) for as long as the buyer, or anyone deriving title from it, carries on a like business. All three conditions of Exception 1 are met, and whether the limits are reasonable is for the court. Refer.

Ahmedabad 'and nowhere else', but the Property is at Mundra (Kachchh), the Lessor is at Gandhidham (Kachchh) and the Lessee at Ghaziabad. No party or property is in Ahmedabad, and the arbitral seat is New Delhi (cl. 18.3). The Gujarat High Court sits there, but it has no ordinary original civil jurisdiction over this lease. Parties cannot confer jurisdiction (A.B.C. Laminart), so this ousts the competent courts. Void, unless facts outside the deed show a cause of action in Ahmedabad.

The lease requires the guarantee to say the bank is 'released from all liability' unless a demand is made within 6 months of termination. That is a discharge on the expiry of a period. Exception 3 saves such a term in a bank guarantee only where the period is at least one year from the specified event; 6 months is less. Void.
A court case must be started within 6 months of the problem arising 'or not at all'. Shortens the 3-year period. Void.

The Lessors' own assessment of restoration cost is final, and the Lessee has 'no right to challenge' it 'before any court, tribunal or arbitral forum'. One party decides and every forum is shut out. Void to that extent.
User clause: the premises only for the Permitted Use (a medical transcription office, cl. I(e)). Restricts use of these premises during the lease, not the Lessee's trade elsewhere.
Interiors to be completed within the Fit-out Period (cl. I(e)), with rent payable from its end if they are not. A commercial term about when rent starts; nothing about claims or courts.
A force majeure notice within 10 days, failing which the party cannot rely on the event as an excuse. No right to sue is extinguished and no liability discharged on the expiry of a period (as PO-63).
Noida courts exclusively, and the premises are in Sector 125, Noida. Courts with jurisdiction anyway; cl. 39 arbitration stands.
The Lessor will not let the floors above and below to a competitor while the Lessee is in occupation. A restriction on how the Lessor deals with its own property, in-term only.
A joint snag list with 30 days to rectify, and it expressly keeps the Lessor liable for defects found later. No right is lost.
User clause: clean and sanitary premises, and no business in the premises other than software development. Restricts use of these premises during the lease, not trade elsewhere.
Forfeiture of Rs. 10 lakh development charges on termination within five years. A s.74 question.
'No liability' unless notice is given within the Claims Notice Period (21 days from awareness, cl. 3A). The other party is discharged on the expiry of a period. Void.

The Pending Claim (cl. 1A) predates the deed and is disputed, so the question 'has already arisen'. It goes to arbitration by a jointly nominated chartered engineer, and the parties agree to abide by the award. Saved by Exception 2.
The Protection Period (cl. 1A) is 3 years after the deed ends, so this is a post-lease restraint on semiconductor design and software development in Noida. No goodwill sold. Void.

No proceedings 'in any court or before any arbitrator' on refund of the deposit, which is left to the Lessor's discretion. One party decides and every forum, including cls. 5A and 12A, is excluded for that class of claims. Void to that extent.
The Lessor alone decides whether the rules were broken; the decision is final and 'cannot be challenged in court or in arbitration'. One party decides and every forum is shut out. Void.

A claim not referred to arbitration within 60 days of the dispute arising is 'deemed to have been abandoned'. The right is extinguished on the expiry of a period, and the 3-year period applies to arbitration through s.43 of the 1996 Act (as PO-03). Void.

The Expert (cl. 1A) is an independent chartered surveyor appointed jointly, and his measurement certificate is final and binding. An agreed way of fixing a fact; courts are not expressly excluded, and cl. 26 arbitration remains. Refer, per the BP-7 approach.
Damages for holding over at twice the rent per day. Whether that is a penalty is a s.74 question.
Exclusion of the Lessors' liability for loss of the Lessee's goods. Limits what is recoverable, not access to court (cf. PO-08, where only the bar on proceedings was void).

Runs during the Term and for 2 years after it, against debt collection in other premises anywhere in Gurgaon. The post-term part is a post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold, and is void. (The in-term part, being business elsewhere, would on its own be a refer.)

During the Lock-out Period (1 year after the Lease Term, cl. 1A), the Lessee may not poach tenants or carry on network equipment business in the same industrial area. A post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold. Void.
The Party of the Second Part cannot sue 'or start arbitration' over damage to its goods. An absolute bar for that class of claims (as PO-08), overriding cl. 35. Void to that extent.

The Claim Expiry Date (cl. 1B) is 4 years from when the payment fell due, longer than the 3-year period (Arts. 52, 55, 113). It does not restrict the right to sue. Not void, though it gives no extra time (s.3 Limitation Act).
Unless claimed within 90 days of year end, the Lessee 'loses that interest for good'. The right is extinguished on the expiry of a period. Void.

The goodwill of the counter is sold to the Lessee (cl. 1A) and the restraint lasts while the buyer carries on the business, but it runs 'in any part of the world'. No specified local limits, so Exception 1 does not apply (as PO-68). Void.

The engineer is nominated by the Lessors, and the Lessee may not dispute his certificate 'before any court, arbitrator or other authority'. A party's nominee plus express exclusion of every forum, so not the BP-7 refer case. Void.
Five years from vacating for a deposit-refund claim. Longer than the 3-year period (Arts. 55/113), so it does not restrict the right to sue. Not void, though the Limitation Act still governs (s.3).

The Lessor fixes the fit-out contribution, and it 'cannot be questioned in any court of law'. One party decides and the courts are excluded, but arbitration is not: Article XXII sends 'all such disputes or differences whatsoever' to arbitration. If XXII reaches this amount a forum remains and the clause is not an absolute bar; if 'final' is read to shut out arbitration too, it is void. The two need reading together (as PO-59). Refer.

The Lessor will not lease its adjoining land to a competitor during the Non-Letting Period (cl. 1A), which runs to 3 years after the Term. During the term it is valid (dealing with its own property); the 3 post-term years are the doubtful part (as PO-43). Refer.

For the Post-Term Restriction Period (15 months after the lease, cl. 1A), the Lessee may not take premises in Bangalore from anyone but the Lessor for its business. A post-lease restraint; that it leaves the Lessor's own premises open does not save it. No goodwill sold. Void.

In-term, but it restrains the Lessee and its group from taking office space in any other building in the technology park. That is business elsewhere, not use of these premises, and the landlord's interest is not apparent from the deed (as PO-11, PO-39). Refer.

Conciliation 'may' be used by agreement, but conciliation does not bind. The clause then says 'no court or tribunal shall have jurisdiction over any matter', which on its words also shuts out the arbitral tribunal. An absolute bar, void. (It contradicts cls. 5A and 12A, which survive it.)
For 2 years after the deed ends, neither party may carry on debt collection in the Building or within 500 m. A post-lease restraint on both, with no goodwill sold. Void.
The Lessor may sue for rent arrears only within 12 months of the rent falling due, against 3 years under Art. 52. Shortens the time to sue, and s.28 protects the Lessor too. Void.

If no defect is pointed out within 10 days of handover, the premises are 'deemed to have been accepted ... in conformity with the agreed specifications'. That deeming takes away the claim for non-conforming premises on the expiry of a period (as PO-14). The inspection step alone would be valid; the deeming words are void.

The Lessee may not maintain 'any suit, arbitration or other legal proceeding' about defects in the Lessors' title, and the claims are given up. An absolute bar for that class of claims, overriding cl. D(vi). Void to that extent.
Interest at 18% on late payments. It does not limit recourse to courts; outside ss.27-28 (as PO-44).

The Lessor's own opinion on whether the Lessee was negligent is final and 'not open to question in any court of law or before any tribunal or arbitrator'. One party decides, and every forum, including the cl. 30 arbitration, is shut out. Void to that extent.

A binding agreement ('shall be referred') to arbitrate under the 1996 Act. That the Lessor alone appoints the sole arbitrator makes the appointment procedure bad (Perkins Eastman, CORE, s.12(5)), but it is still an arbitration agreement. Saved by Exception 1.

The payment date is ordinary. But during the 36-month lock-in the Lessee may not relocate operations to, or expand in, any other premises in Bangalore. That is an in-term restraint on carrying on business elsewhere, not on use of these premises, and the landlord's commercial interest is not apparent from the deed. Refer.
The Exclusivity Undertaking (cl. 1A) runs for 2 years after the deed ends, within 3 km. A post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold. Void.
